patterns.source: project/paper.txt (the project's own paper, used as a Level-0 structural exemplar; no external exemplar corpus was available under this run's no-web constraint)
patterns.rhetorical_purpose: compress the whole study into context, method, headline results and their meaning in one paragraph
move_sequence: state the limiting condition of prior work (homogeneous, narrow settings)
name the artifact and its scale (18 datasets)
name what was tested (10 systems, 5 architectures)
give the headline comparative result with a qualifier (robust baseline; best performer at high cost)
state the practical meaning (room for improvement in generalization)
point to the released artifact
patterns.reader_question_answered: What is the problem, what did you build/do, what did you find, and where can I get it?
patterns.assumed_knowledge: general neural IR and Transformer-based retrieval vocabulary (this paper is written for IR specialists, mode A, not mode B; adapted for this paper's mode-B audience)
patterns.transition_behavior: each sentence's last clause becomes the next sentence's opening topic (e.g. 'evaluate 10 ... systems' leads into 'Our results show ...')
patterns.evidence_placement: one or two headline numbers only (7-18 points; +11%-scale contrasts implied); full tables held for the body
patterns.result_interpretation_pattern: result stated with its qualifier in the same clause ('robust baseline', 'at high computational costs') rather than as a bare number
patterns.limitation_framing: folded into the closing sentence as a forward-looking need ('considerable room for improvement') rather than a separate hedge
patterns.contribution_framing: framed as an artifact ('we introduce BEIR') plus a finding, not as a list of bullet contributions

patterns.rhetorical_purpose: state one numbered finding per paragraph, each with its own interpretation
move_sequence: bold micro-headline stating the finding as a claim
the supporting comparison with numbers
one sentence on what it means or why it matters
patterns.reader_question_answered: What is the single most important thing to take from this comparison?
patterns.assumed_knowledge: the architecture taxonomy and the metric, both introduced earlier in the paper
patterns.transition_behavior: findings are numbered (1-7) rather than linked by transition words; each is a self-contained unit
patterns.evidence_placement: numbers appear in the same paragraph as the claim they support, immediately after the claim sentence
patterns.result_interpretation_pattern: what happened, then a one-clause reason or consequence, rarely more than 3-4 sentences per finding
patterns.figure_table_integration: each numbered finding points to the shared results table rather than repeating a sub-table

patterns.rhetorical_purpose: state each limitation as a named category with a one-paragraph justification and forward pointer
move_sequence: name the limitation category in bold
state what was not covered and why (often a real constraint, e.g. transformer length limits)
point to what future work could do about it
patterns.reader_question_answered: Which claims are bounded, and by what?
patterns.assumed_knowledge: the design choices already described earlier in the paper
patterns.evidence_placement: no new numbers; refers back to design choices already described in Methods
patterns.limitation_framing: each limitation is a scope boundary on the method, not a hedge on a specific claim's confidence -- this paper's Limitations section instead ties each one to the specific claims it bounds, per section_rules.md

patterns.rhetorical_purpose: motivate a secondary study that qualifies the main comparison, without undermining the paper's own headline claims
move_sequence: name the general phenomenon (selection bias in pooled annotation) with a citation
give a concrete instance in the paper's own data (TREC-COVID)
describe the controlled fix (manual re-annotation, blind to source system)
report the before/after numbers
state the qualified conclusion (bias exists and matters, but does not overturn the main comparison; it is a call for better test-collection design)
patterns.reader_question_answered: Could the main comparison's ranking be an artifact of how the test data was built, rather than a true capability gap?
patterns.assumed_knowledge: pooling and relevance-judgement construction (introduced within the same section)
patterns.transition_behavior: explicit causal chain, each step justified before the next is taken
patterns.evidence_placement: a small, cleanly-structured table (Hole@10 and before/after nDCG@10) immediately after the procedure is described
patterns.result_interpretation_pattern: full Result Interpretation Chain: what was measured, what happened, size of the effect per system, and an explicit statement of what it does and does not overturn
patterns.figure_table_integration: table takeaway stated in prose before and after the table appears
patterns.limitation_framing: explicitly scoped to the one dataset studied, not generalized to all of BEIR without qualification
patterns.contribution_framing: framed as strengthening the benchmark's honesty, not as undermining it

patterns.rhetorical_purpose: make the research gap feel necessary by naming exactly what each prior effort does not cover
move_sequence: name the prior work and its scope
give the specific numeric limitation (task count, dataset count, corpus size)
state directly what it does not test
patterns.reader_question_answered: Why isn't an existing benchmark already sufficient?
patterns.assumed_knowledge: none beyond what the paper has already introduced
patterns.transition_behavior: each prior work gets its own short paragraph, organized by what it lacks, not narrated chronologically
patterns.evidence_placement: specific counts (e.g. '5 out of eight datasets are from Wikipedia') rather than vague characterization
patterns.contribution_framing: the gap statement is immediately followed, in the next section, by the paper's own selection criteria answering exactly those lacks
